name: postgres
title: PostgreSQL — durable actors under load
summary: Bank accounts as durable actors in PostgreSQL: concurrent transfers from pgbench, money conserved at every sample, timers, an outbox, and a database restart in the middle.
description: Runs on the PostgreSQL instance of the PostgreSQL binding (mise run pg:start; the page detects it live and offers to start it). 2,000 account actors live in tinyactors.actors. pgbench clients send transfer events; an account that can afford it debits itself and sends a deposit to the other account — an actor-to-actor event, processed in the same transaction when the receiver is free, otherwise left in its inbox (SKIP LOCKED) for tinyactors.run(). Two more pgbench processes are the application's workers, as a deployment would run them: a scheduler calling tinyactors.run() (due timers — every account files a statement every 5 s — and deferred deposits) and an audit worker draining the outbox with claim() and ack() (large transfers are reported to an audit service). Every second the bench only measures: one snapshot query checks that money is conserved — balances plus deposits still in inboxes — and one event's end-to-end latency is probed. A hot spot puts 3 accounts under heavy contention; a restart of PostgreSQL shows that nothing is lost: balances, queued deposits and timers survive. Tune with --param accounts, clients.

hot-spot.title: Hot spot (20 s)
hot-spot.description: 8 more clients transfer between 3 accounts: their row locks serialize them, cascades skip them

restart.title: Restart PostgreSQL
restart.description: A fast shutdown and start: committed balances, queued deposits and timers survive; the load resumes
